# Space Atrapos - Tutorial

# lessons | Lessons
First steps, one topic at a time: what to do, in the order you'll need it. The [Pilot's guide](doc:start) has every detail; the Controls book lists every key.

## t-getting-started | Getting Started
[b]Welcome, pilot.[/b]

![](shot:space_hud)

You fly a light fighter in a sector full of raiders. Destroy enemy ships, collect what they drop, sell it at stations, and spend your drachmas on better equipment and technology.

[b]Your first steps[/b]
1. Click anywhere in empty space to fly there.
2. Click a red-marked enemy ship to attack it.
3. Fly over the glowing loot it drops to collect it.
4. You start in orbit above [b]Amnissos[/b] - click its LAND button to explore it - near [b]Kephala Outpost[/b]. Land on Amnissos first: [b]Kilon Alios[/b], the hooded wanderer by the landing pad, gives you the story. Click a station to dock, sell loot, and pick up extra jobs under [b]Missions[/b]. A hollow [b]yellow triangle[/b] over their head marks whoever has a quest for you.
5. Press [b]Tab[/b] any time to open this Ship Computer.

## t-the-galaxy | The Galaxy
[b]New Hellas[/b]: [b]fifty-eight star systems[/b], linked by [b]jump gates[/b] at their edges. Each has a star at its centre, planets on slow orbits, stations, asteroid fields - and an owner.

![](shot:computer_galaxy)

[b]Four star empires[/b] rebuilt the Greek civilisations among the stars: the [b]Athenian League[/b] (your home), the [b]Spartan Hegemony[/b], the [b]Minoan Thalassocracy[/b] and the [b]Mycenaean Kingdoms[/b]. The [b]Sea Peoples[/b] are raiders who prey on everyone. Each empire has its own ships, stations and architecture.

Empires make [b]war and peace[/b] over time and fight over border systems, which can change hands. Systems go through [b]states[/b] - Boom, Bust, Famine, Outbreak, Civil Unrest, Pirate Raids, Expansion - that move prices and danger. Follow it all in the [b]galactic news[/b].

[b]G[/b] opens the [b]Galaxy map[/b]: click a system and [b]Plot route[/b] - your course is set to the right gate, and after each jump to the next one. Fly into a gate to jump.

## t-trading | Trading
Every station has a live [b]Market[/b]. Stations [b]produce[/b] some goods and [b]need[/b] others; prices follow supply - cheap where goods are made, dear where they're scarce.

![](shot:station_market)

Production chains link the stations: a station short of its inputs (shown in red) slows down - and pays more for them. System states and wars shift demand too (weapons, fuel and medicine sell high in wartime).

[b]NPC traders[/b] fly these routes, each with their own cargo and drachmas - and so can you. Your hold size depends on your ship and its cargo racks.

[b]Sea Peoples raiders[/b] board disabled freighters and steal their cargo. Destroy them and the stolen goods spill out for you to collect - plus a bounty from the system's owner.

## t-empires-reputation | Empires & Reputation
You answer to no empire. Your [b]reputation[/b] with each of them - and with the [b]Independents[/b] - is all that counts, from [b]Hostile[/b] through Unfriendly, Neutral, Cordial and Friendly to [b]Allied[/b] (the station's [b]Reputation[/b] tab shows it).

![](shot:station_reputation)

- It [b]rises[/b] with missions at their stations, trading there (every 10,000 dr bought or sold: +1 - reputation grows slowly) and hunting Sea Peoples raiders in their space.
- It [b]falls[/b] when you attack their ships: a little for the first shot at one, more for each one destroyed. It takes several to make an enemy - and a bad name fades back toward Neutral with time.
- [b]Hostile[/b]: their warships attack you and their stations refuse you. Better standing brings better missions (Trusted, Honoured), better prices and bigger bounties.

Most stations in a system belong to the empire holding it. The rest are [b]independent[/b] free ports (neutral with everyone, out of every war), an ally's [b]outpost[/b] (opened with the owner's leave) or a [b]forward base[/b] of an empire at war with the owner, wearing the system down to take it. When a system falls, its stations change hands.

## t-ships-outfitting | Ships & Outfitting
The [b]Shipyard[/b] at each station sells its empire's designs - fighters, gunships, frigates, cruisers, dreadnoughts, freighters, mining barges and explorers. Your old ship is traded in.

![](shot:station_outfitting)

Each ship has [b]hardpoints[/b] (weapons), [b]internal slots[/b] and [b]utility mounts[/b]. [b]Outfitting[/b] sells modules rated [b]E[/b] (cheap) to [b]A[/b] (best): shield generators, hull reinforcement, cargo racks, thrusters, shield cell banks, gimballed mounts and shield amplifiers - plus the weapons and active systems.

## t-comms | Comms
Press [b]H[/b] (or Shift + right-click > Hail) to call your target or the nearest ship. Traders share trade tips, patrols report on the war, and Sea Peoples raiders demand tribute.

Station dockmasters, empire liaisons and mission givers greet you in person - the peoples of these star nations are descended from dinosaurs.

## t-main-quest | Main Quest
[b]The Thread of Ariadne[/b] (talk to [b]Kilon Alios[/b] by the landing pad on Amnissos to take it) is the story of the Atrapos sector - a mystery that leads back to the Minoans of Bronze Age Crete.

![](shot:computer_quest)

• The current objective is shown at the [b]top of the screen[/b], and a [b]gold star or arrow[/b] on the minimap points the way.
• Story conversations pause the game. Click, press Space or Enter to continue, or press Skip. Esc opens the Esc menu on top.
• Some steps ask you to bring items to a station - just dock there with them and they're handed over automatically.
• Story bosses show a large health bar at the top of the screen.
• Open the [b]QUEST[/b] tab (Tab) to see the chapters and re-read every conversation in the journal.
• Each step unlocks real history in the Encyclopedia under [b]Lore: Ancient Greece[/b].

## t-flying | Flying
[b]Moving[/b]
• Click empty space: the ship turns and flies to that point, slowing down as it arrives. A ring marks the destination.
• Hold the left button and drag to steer continuously; the cursor hides while you steer.

[b]Camera & minimap[/b]
• The camera follows your ship.
• The round minimap (top right) shows you as an arrow, enemies as red dots, and stations as coloured diamonds.
• Stations off the minimap appear as coloured [b]arrows on its edge[/b] with their distance (e.g. 5.2k).

## t-combat | Combat
[b]Attacking[/b]
• Click an enemy to lock on - red brackets and its class name appear.
• If it's out of range, your ship [b]flies into range automatically[/b], then fires on its own.
• Keep clicking empty space to manoeuvre while firing; the lock stays.
• Shift + right-click and choose [b]Stop attacking[/b] to stop firing.
• Click a [b]neutral[/b] ship once to follow it; click it again to attack.
• [b]Right-click[/b] an asteroid to prospect it: what it's made of and where its veins run - then hold the button on it to cut a vein, keeping its heat in the green. Right-click empty space for the [b]probe scanner[/b] (outfitters sell it): launch probes on the map, draw them in tight and analyze to locate the system's [b]signal sources[/b], ships, planets and stations - then press ENTER at a located beacon (distress calls, pirate attacks, wrecks, alien creatures, anomalies to scan, deadly anomaly fields).
• Hits that reach your hull damage your ship's parts: their [b]afflictions[/b] show as icons under your health bars, and the first always stops your hull mending itself until they're repaired. No shot is certain - yours or theirs.

![](shot:space_combat)

[b]Enemies[/b]
• They patrol until you come close (or shoot them), then chase and fire.
• Every class behaves differently - see the Encyclopedia.
• If they lose you they give up and return to patrol.
• Enemies have [b]shields[/b] too (orange bar, red-orange glow when hit). Shields soak damage first and recharge if you stop shooting for a few seconds - keep up the pressure.

[b]Defence[/b]
• [b]Shields[/b] (blue bar) absorb damage first and recharge a few seconds after the last hit.
• [b]Hull[/b] (green bar) only repairs at stations, with repair kits, or with Nanite tech.
• If the hull reaches 0 your ship is destroyed - restart or load a save.

## t-repairs | Repairs: parts and surgery
Hits that get through to your hull can damage a [b]part[/b] of your ship - the engines, the sensors, the reactor... - and a damaged part works less well: slower engines, weaker shields, a fuel leak. The log tells you which part was hit.

[b]Fixing it yourself[/b]
1. Open the Ship Computer ([b]Tab[/b]) on the [b]Repair[/b] tab, and click the damaged part.
2. Click the casing's bolts to undo them - opposite ones in turn, never two neighbours, or the casing warps.
3. Take the [b]Scanner[/b] and sweep the part: rest the lens on what lights up to mark the fault. Each kind of fault shows in its own mode.
4. Fix each one with its tool: weld cracks slowly, solder burnt wiring (cut the power first!), seal leaks while the pressure's low, tune misaligned parts, and swap wrecked components for spare parts.
5. Bolt the casing back on.

Watch the [b]vitals[/b]: too much heat cuts the welder out and undoes half the weld. Nothing you do at the table damages the part - only hits do. Your automaton is mended in the same tab, on foot or in space - as a body: its anatomy in four layers (muscles, veins, nerves, skeleton), a scalpel to cut down to what lies under the muscle, sutures, a bone fuser, clamps. Rather not? Any station's technicians fix everything for a price.

![](shot:repair_bay)

## t-neutral-ships | Neutral Ships
Civilian ships - [b]freighters[/b], [b]explorers[/b] and [b]mining barges[/b] - fly between stations and explore open space.

• They are shown with [b]green[/b] shields and green minimap dots; locking on shows a [b]yellow[/b] bracket marked NEUTRAL.
• They [b]never attack you first[/b].
• Pirates hunt them. Neutrals fight back, so you can help them - or scavenge the wreckage of their fights. Loot drops whoever destroys a ship.
• You [b]can[/b] attack them, but they fight back and stay hostile to you for 30 seconds (orange bracket and dot).
• Only your own kills count toward missions.
• Nobody fights inside a station's safe zone.

## t-mining | Mining
Five [b]asteroid fields[/b] float between the stations (grey dots on the minimap).

![](shot:mining)

[b]How to mine[/b]
• Click an asteroid - white brackets show its type and how much ore is left.
• Your ship flies into range and cuts it with its red [b]mining beam[/b] (whatever weapon is selected). The ore it cuts off is pulled to your ship.
• Rocks are big - mining one out takes a long while. It shrinks as you mine it and [b]shatters when depleted - gone for good[/b]: asteroids don't come back, and each system remembers what's left.
• Civilian [b]mining barges[/b] work the fields too, then sell their ore at the stations.

[b]Ores[/b]
• [b]Iron[/b] - brown rock, rusty veins. Common, 6 dr.
• [b]Titanium[/b] - blue-grey rock, glowing cyan veins. 16 dr.
• [b]Platinum[/b] - dark rock, glowing gold veins. Rare, 45 dr.

Sell ore at any station, or deliver it for Salvage Request missions. Heavier weapons mine faster; mining barges (neutral) prospect the fields too.

## t-planets | Planets
Every planet of the home system can be visited: [b]Akrotiri[/b] (volcanic world - no one lives there), [b]Amnissos[/b] (ocean world), its moon [b]Kamares[/b], [b]Ida[/b] (ice world) and [b]Dikte[/b], a gas giant with no surface - you land on platforms in its clouds.

![](shot:surface_walk)

[b]Landing[/b]
• When a landable planet is on screen, a [b]LAND[/b] button appears over it - click it.
• You can't land while an enemy is attacking you.

[b]On the surface[/b] (isometric view)
• Click to walk, or hold the button to keep walking toward the cursor. Water and crevasses block the way.
• [b]Colony outposts[/b] - concrete foundations with landing pads and structures (reactors, radar dishes, hangars, turrets...). Click a structure to inspect it; they block your path, and fade when you walk behind them.
• [b]Minoan palace[/b] - walk in through its sliding doors: frescoed halls, red columns and a mosaic hall, built from the Minoan tile set.
• [b]Minoan citizens[/b] - triceratops guards with laser rifles, and androids in a triceratops's image armed with laser rifles, laser bows or the labrys (the double axe). They patrol the streets and shoot anything hostile; click one to hear what they say (the translation appears in the event log).
• [b]Buildings[/b] - walk in through their sliding doors and explore. Each planet has a large [b]Minoan palace[/b] (frescoed rooms and a pillared hall with a mosaic floor), plus Minoan [b]warehouses[/b] and a [b]temple[/b] where the citizens live. Roofs and front walls fade when you're inside or behind them.
• The minimap shows the planet surface while you're down there.

[b]Leaving[/b]
Click your landed ship or the [b]LEAVE PLANET[/b] button. You return to orbit exactly as you left it.

## t-skills | Skills: fists, the leap, spells
On a planet your automaton fights with more than its rifle. Its [b]skills[/b] sit on the toolbar (keys 1-9) next to the rifle and the medicine; at first: [b]4 Pygmachia[/b] (boxing), [b]5 Hermes' Leap[/b], [b]6 Phlox[/b] (a fireball).

![](shot:skills_fight)

[b]Fighting hand to hand[/b]
• Press [b]4[/b] (or click the slot): the automaton puts the rifle away. Click a pirate - it runs up and throws its blows one after the other: jab, cross... Each blow staggers the enemy; finishers knock it flat.
• Slot [b]1[/b] takes the rifle up again.
• Pirates fight back with their own fists and feet when you're close - and some charge you.

[b]The leap[/b]
• Point the mouse somewhere and press [b]5[/b]: a flip through the air to that spot. Shots fired at you while you're up miss - leap in on a rifleman, or out of trouble.

[b]Spells[/b]
• Point at an enemy and press [b]6[/b]: a ball of fire that bursts where it lands and leaves them burning. Spells and techniques have a cooldown (the dark curtain on the slot), and every skill costs [b]stamina[/b] - carry food and Energy Drinks.

![](shot:skill_book)

[b]Levels and the Spell Book[/b]
• Fighting earns experience (the thin bar over the toolbar). Each level gives a [b]skill point[/b].
• Press [b]K[/b] for the Spell Book: spend points to [b]learn[/b] new skills (more martial styles, a sweep, a flying kick, a beam, the thunderbolt, a dome of force, spectral fighters) or to [b]raise the rank[/b] of the ones you have. Drag a skill's icon onto the toolbar, or hover it and press 1-9.

## t-weapons-systems | Weapons & Systems
The toolbar at the bottom has 9 slots for your weapons and systems. Click a slot or press its number (1-9). You choose what goes where: in the Ship Computer's inventory (I), hover a weapon, a system or repair kits and press 1-9; right-click a slot to empty it. At first:

[b]Weapons (select one)[/b]
1 - [b]Pulse Cannon[/b]: fast, accurate, unlimited.
2 - [b]Plasma Cannon[/b]: slow but very heavy hits.
3 - [b]Missiles[/b]: longest range, homing, uses missile ammo.

[b]Systems (activate)[/b]
4 - [b]Afterburner[/b]: big speed boost for 3 seconds.
5 - [b]Shield Booster[/b]: instantly restores 60 shields.
6 - [b]Repair Kit[/b]: restores 40 hull, uses one kit.

Locked slots (padlock) must be bought at a station first. A dark overlay with a number shows a cooldown.

## t-loot-cargo | Loot & Cargo
Destroyed ships always drop [b]drachmas[/b] and often [b]items[/b]. Bigger ships drop more and rarer loot.

![](shot:salvage)

• Loot drifts in space and is pulled in when you fly close.
• It disappears after a minute (it blinks before vanishing).

[b]Items[/b]
• Scrap Metal, Energy Cells, Alien Alloy - sell them at stations.
• [b]Data Cores[/b] - rare and valuable; also needed for top-tier tech.
• Missiles and Repair Kits - go straight into your supplies.

Open the [b]Inventory[/b] tab (or press I) to see your cargo.

## t-stations | Stations
Four stations are scattered across the sector. Each has a [b]safe zone[/b] (dashed ring) where enemies won't attack you.

[b]Docking[/b]
• Click a station: your ship flies there and docks automatically.
• Or fly close and press [b]E[/b].
• Docking pauses the game and recharges your shields for free.

[b]Facilities[/b]
• [b]Repair[/b] - fix your hull for drachmas.
• [b]Buy[/b] - missiles, repair kits and new equipment.
• [b]Sell[/b] - turn loot into drachmas.
• [b]Main Quests[/b] - how far you are in the story, The Thread of Ariadne (Kilon Alios on Amnissos gives it).
• [b]Missions[/b] - take jobs for pay and reputation.

Press E or Undock to leave.

## t-missions | Missions
Each station's [b]Missions[/b] tab offers eight jobs. You can run up to [b]five at once[/b]; active missions are listed under the minimap.

![](shot:station_missions)

• [b]Pirate Sweep[/b] - destroy a number of enemies of any kind.
• [b]Hunt[/b] - destroy a specific ship class. Hunted classes show up more often while the mission is active. Big targets also pay a Data Core.
• [b]Courier[/b] - dock at another station to deliver a package.
• [b]Supply Run[/b] - buy trade goods at a market and deliver them to another station.
• [b]Salvage Request / Mining Contract[/b] - bring salvage or ore back to the issuing station and press Turn In.
• [b]Survey[/b] - fly to an uncharted point (marked on your map) to scan it.

Missions come in four tiers - [b]Routine, Trusted, Honoured, Hero[/b] - needing reputation 0, 10, 25 and 50 with the station's empire; the better ones pay more. Ones you aren't trusted with yet are [b]greyed out[/b]. Every mission you finish raises your reputation with that empire (more for the higher tiers). Kill, courier, supply and survey missions pay out automatically when completed. You can abandon a mission at any station.

## t-tech-tree | Tech Tree
The [b]Tech Tree[/b] tab lets you permanently upgrade your ship with drachmas.

![](shot:computer_tech)

• Five branches: Hull, Shields, Weapons, Engines and Salvage.
• Each branch has three tiers; you must research them in order.
• The top tier of each branch also needs [b]Data Cores[/b].

Upgrades apply immediately - bigger hull and shields, faster regeneration, more damage, speed and range, and better loot.

## t-saving | Saving
Press [b]Esc[/b] to pause and open the menu.

• [b]Save Game[/b] stores your ship, drachmas, cargo, equipment, tech, missions and the enemies around you.
• [b]Load Game[/b] restores the last save (also available from the title screen and after your ship is destroyed).
• [b]Settings[/b] lets you change the resolution or go fullscreen.

Loot still floating in space is not saved - collect it first!

## t-developer-tools | Developer Tools
Shift + right-click in space (right-click on a planet) for the developer menu.

[b]Developer Mode[/b]
• [b]Dialogue[/b]: pick a quest stage; edit its objective, chapter, station, required items, enemies, rewards, lore unlocks and every dialogue line (add, delete, reorder, preview).
• [b]Quest[/b]: jump to any stage, complete the current objective, reset the quest, unlock all lore, rename chapters.
• [b]Lore[/b] and [b]Interactions[/b]: edit encyclopedia entries and citizen lines.
• [b]Player[/b]: drachmas, Data Cores, repairs, equipment, tech.
Edits apply immediately. [b]Save to file[/b] writes [b]data/main_quest.json[/b] and [b]data/interactions.json[/b] - plain text files you can also edit directly.

[b]Level Editor[/b]
• On planets: paint terrain, draw Minoan palaces, warehouses and temples, place outpost structures and draw foundations / landing pads, click walls to switch plain / window / door, place columns, citizens and scenery, erase. [b]Save layout[/b] writes [b]data/planets/<planet>.json[/b], used instead of the generated planet.
• In space: place enemy and neutral ships and asteroids, erase. [b]Save layout[/b] writes [b]data/space.json[/b], used by new games instead of random placement.
• Wheel zooms, WASD / arrows / middle-drag pan. [b]Revert to generated[/b] deletes the saved layout.
